notes.subject: language
notes.text: Traditional Chinese-style characters with many strokes, with no kana mixed in.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles nearly always wear black and yellow diagonal stripes running all the way down to the ground; the yellow looks orange.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Drives on the right.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Double yellow centre line with single white edge lines; narrow roads may use one dashed yellow line.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Roads with white edge lines and no centre line at all are very common.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Red edge lines marking no parking are common, especially in cities, and almost unique.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are black arrows on yellow.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Traffic mirrors with orange hoods at junctions and bends.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black rectangular bollards holding two or three round reflectors.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Lollipop-shaped reflectors on guardrails, like those seen in Japan.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Concrete drainage ditches line many roads.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Box-shaped distribution transformers, usually dark green or grey, especially in cities.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Blue plaques on poles with letters and numbers act as precise coordinates.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Boxy buildings with white-tiled walls, cramped multi-storey housing, and light-green tin sheds.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A black Generation 3 car with a long antenna and central red brake light, or one with an enormous blur but normal camera height.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat to rolling farmland in the west, with forested mountains across the central two-thirds.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Area codes run 02 to 08, rising toward the south; mobile numbers start 09.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Several far-off island groups have coverage, including two near the mainland coast of China and one in the middle of the strait.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A long thin valley on the east coast: flat plains between densely forested mountains west and east.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Open rice plain with mountains to north, west and south but almost none to the east; villas by the fields.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Fuzzy-leaved roadside trees, red-tinged soil, traditional small houses and red-and-white striped lampposts.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Rows of cook pines by the road, cream-coloured houses and blue outer lines found nowhere else.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Areca (betel nut) palms are common in central and southern mountains; neat plantations on flat land are mostly in Pingtung.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Fish farms right by the coast, mostly in the southwest counties.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Tropical islands off the southeast with coconut palms, lush cliffs and run-down concrete pavement.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Yellow guardrails along the western half of the cross-island highway in the east.
